steps.name: AXIOM
steps.description: A0 AXIOM: a single prism, 80.5 x 9.9 x 19.3 m, labelled BLOCK

steps.name: R_LIFT
steps.description: A1 R_LIFT: SPLIT-Z at 2.50 m. The lower part is emptied to a colonnade of CO.PIL (3 rows x 23 lines) and the upper part relabelled MASS: the ground plane is given away, which is the first political act of the building. Graph: one node becomes two, joined by a 'supports' edge.

steps.name: R_STACK
steps.description: A2 R_STACK: repeated SPLIT-Z of MASS into 6 storey bands of 2.80 m, each a slab band + a storey volume, closed by SL.ROOF. Graph: a vertical chain of 'above' edges - stacking is the only rule so far that makes the graph three-dimensional, and R_LCELL/R_UCELL will later exploit it.

steps.name: R_BAY (bay / party-wall pair)
steps.description: A3 R_BAY (the bay / party-wall pair): SPLIT-X of a storey band on a 3.66 m rhythm. The rule is a PAIR because neither half is meaningful alone: each cut produces a bay slab AND the party wall on the cut line, and the column CO.RECT is absorbed into that wall, splitting it into pieces. Graph: 22 bay nodes per level, chained by blind 'party wall' edges - adjacency without access, which is exactly what a party wall means.

steps.name: R_CORRIDOR
steps.description: A4 R_CORRIDOR: SPLIT-Y of levels L1, L4 into a 1.80 m common corridor on the south and the dwelling band on the north, with DV.WALL.CORR (door notch per bay) on the cut. Graph: the corridor nodes form an open chain - the 'internal street'. This is the level at which the whole social programme is decided.

steps.name: R_LCELL / R_UCELL
steps.description: A5 R_LCELL / R_UCELL (one rule, one parameter): a run of stacked bays is merged into a single dwelling whose SECTION is the bay rectangle minus the corridor notch. K: 2 levels, corridor at index 0 -> section L; F: 3 levels, corridor at index 1 -> section U; E: 1 level, no corridor notch -> flat (the end units beyond the cores). The K cell is an L: two levels, corridor at the bottom, so the upper level runs the full 9.90 m depth over the corridor. The F cell is a U: three levels, corridor through the MIDDLE, so the dwelling has a full-depth level below AND above the street and only a narrow hall band beside it. One corridor therefore serves three floors. Graph: the stacked bay nodes COLLAPSE into one dwelling node with a single 'entrance door' edge to the corridor - the section rule is visible in the graph as a change of node count, which is what we want to drive variants from. The END UNITS are the degenerate case of the same production - levels = 1, no notch - which is the cheapest possible proof that L, U and flat are one rule and not three.

steps.name: R_CORE
steps.description: A6 R_CORE: two bays (lines 2 and 19) are relabelled as vertical cores - CI.FLIGHT pairs + SP.STAIRWELL. Graph: the only nodes carrying VERTICAL edges. Until this rule the graph is a set of horizontal chains; after it the graph is genuinely three-dimensional. The core also CARRIES THE STREET: because it interrupts the corridor, it takes a door on each side, so the chain runs corridor - stairwell - corridor rather than breaking into two dangling halves. The end units and the dwellings beside the core are entered from the same lobby.

steps.name: R_FACADE (facade split)
steps.description: A7 R_FACADE (facade split): every envelope panel is SPLIT-Z at 1.00 m into EN.SPAND below and EN.WIN.RIBBON above, the pane running from end to end of the block. Two things matter grammatically: (i) the split height is a parameter - at spandrel = 0 the same rule yields the condenser's EN.WIN.CURT, so ribbon and curtain wall are ONE rule, not two; (ii) the pane is NOT subdivided by the bay rule, so the facade is deliberately out of step with the structure. A per-bay window would generate a different architecture with the same plan. The graph is unchanged: the facade split adds no nodes, only exterior faces - envelope is style, not topology.

steps.name: R_END + R_ROOF
steps.description: A8 R_END + R_ROOF: EN.WALL.END terminates the repetition along x (a blind gable - the rule that says 'stop'), with SL.BALC.SEMI attached to its outer face on L2-L5, and the stack is closed by parapet and penthouse. Graph: one terminal node on top of a core.

B.name: SOCIAL CONDENSER
B.scope: the communal block + the bridge that composes the two

steps.name: AXIOM
steps.description: B0 AXIOM: a second, separate prism - the social condenser. It is a SEPARATE GRAMMAR because its rules are different in kind: the block subdivides a repetitive frame, the condenser merges levels into a single collective volume. Same operations, opposite direction.

steps.name: R_STACK
steps.description: B1 R_STACK: the same SPLIT-Z as A2, 4 storeys.

steps.name: R_MERGE (condenser)
steps.description: B2 R_MERGE (the social condenser rule): delete an intermediate slab and UNION the two storeys into one double-height volume - gymnasium / dining / library. Graph: two nodes collapse into one of HIGH degree. That is the graph-theoretic definition of a 'social condenser': not a room type but a node whose degree is out of proportion to the rest of the graph.

steps.name: R_GALLERY
steps.description: B3 R_GALLERY: SUBTRACT a curved void from a slab inside the hall, giving SL.GALL. Graph: a node adjacent to the hall by an OPEN edge (no wall, no door) - the relation that makes a gallery a gallery rather than a room.

steps.name: R_FACADE (curtain)
steps.description: B4 R_FACADE (spandrel = 0): the SAME facade split as A7 with the split height driven to zero, so the whole east face becomes one storey-high pane per level. Ribbon and curtain wall are one rule with one parameter - this is the strongest evidence that the two grammars share an alphabet.

steps.name: R_CORE
steps.description: B5 R_CORE: a core strip is attached to the north face (ATTACH on a face port, not a split). It overshoots the roof by one level, which is what gives the condenser its roof terrace.

steps.name: R_BRIDGE
steps.description: B6 R_BRIDGE (the composition rule): a single volume at L1 linking the condenser core to the block's corridor. In the graph it is a CUT VERTEX - delete it and the design falls into two components. The two grammars are therefore composed by exactly one production, which is why they can be developed, and varied, independently.

rule_cards.title: facade split  panel -> EN.SPAND + EN.WIN.RIBBON (continuous)
rule_cards.note:
SPLIT-Z at h=1.00. The pane is NOT cut by the bay rule: one pane spans the whole facade.
h is a parameter: h=0 gives EN.WIN.CURT (the condenser). Graph: unchanged.

rule_cards.title: bay / party-wall PAIR  band -> 2 bays + party wall + column
rule_cards.note:
SPLIT-X at 3.66. Inseparable pair: the cut yields two bay slabs AND the party wall on the
cut line, with CO.RECT absorbed into it (so the wall arrives in pieces). Graph: 1 node -> 2,
joined by a BLIND edge - adjacent, not connected.

rule_cards.title: corridor insertion  bay -> SP.CORRIDOR + dwelling band
rule_cards.note:
SPLIT-Y at 1.80 with DV.WALL.CORR on the cut. Graph: corridor nodes form an OPEN chain
(the internal street); each dwelling gets exactly one 'entrance door' edge to it.

rule_cards.title: L-section cell (K-type): 2 levels, corridor at the BOTTOM
rule_cards.note:
2 stacked bays + the corridor at level 0 MERGE into ONE dwelling. The section is the
bay rectangle minus the corridor notch -> L. The pierced level keeps only a
1.58 m hall band beside the street. Graph: the stacked bay nodes COLLAPSE into one dwelling
node; one corridor serves two floors.

rule_cards.title: U-section cell (F-type): 3 levels, corridor in the MIDDLE
rule_cards.note:
3 stacked bays + the corridor at level 1 MERGE into ONE dwelling. The section is the
bay rectangle minus the corridor notch -> U. The pierced level keeps only a
1.58 m hall band beside the street. Graph: the stacked bay nodes COLLAPSE into one dwelling
node; one corridor serves three floors.

rule_cards.title: social condenser  two storeys -> one double-height SP.HALL
rule_cards.note:
The INVERSE of R_STACK: delete the intermediate slab and UNION the storeys. Graph: two nodes
collapse into one of high degree - the graph definition of a social condenser.

variants.note: as built: K-type, 2 levels, corridor at the bottom
as built: F-type, 3 levels, corridor through the middle
unbuilt: corridor at the TOP - the L flipped, access over the dwelling
unbuilt: 4 levels, corridor at level 1 - a skip-stop section, one street per four floors
